senses.meaning: Phân bón
examples: Farmers apply fertilizer to their fields every spring.
Excessive use of chemical fertilizers can damage soil quality.
Organic fertilizers like compost are increasingly popular.

senses.meaning: Đất (tầng đất trồng trọt, đất canh tác)
examples: The soil in this region is rich and fertile.
Heavy rain can erode valuable topsoil.
The plants need well-drained soil to thrive.

senses.meaning: Màu mỡ, phì nhiêu (đất); có khả năng sinh sản (người/động vật)
examples: The Nile Delta has some of the most fertile land in Africa.
Fertile soil is essential for growing high-quality crops.
The couple was relieved to learn she was still fertile.

note: Đối lập: 'barren' (cằn cỗi, vô sinh). 'Fertile ground' nghĩa bóng = môi trường thuận lợi cho sự phát triển.

senses.meaning: Ruộng bậc thang
examples: Terraced fields carved into the hillside are a common sight in northern Vietnam.
The terraced fields of Mù Cang Chải are a UNESCO-recognised landscape.
Farmers created terraced fields to cultivate rice on steep mountain slopes.

senses.meaning: Mùa vụ, vụ mùa; lứa sản phẩm hoặc người
examples: This year's wheat crop was the best in a decade.
Crops failed across the region due to severe drought.
A new crop of graduates entered the job market this spring.

senses.meaning: Cắt ngắn (tóc, ảnh); (động vật) gặm cỏ
examples: She cropped her hair short before the summer.
The photo was cropped to remove the busy background.
Sheep were quietly cropping the grass on the hillside.

note: 'Crop up' = xuất hiện bất ngờ (phrasal verb).

senses.meaning: Nghề cá, ngư trường; trại nuôi cá
examples: The cod fishery off the coast collapsed in the 1990s due to overfishing.
He works in a local fishery processing factory.
Sustainable management of fisheries is crucial for long-term food security.

senses.meaning: Ấp trứng; ủ (vi khuẩn, bệnh); nuôi dưỡng (ý tưởng, dự án)
examples: The hen incubated her eggs for three weeks before they hatched.
The disease incubates for five to ten days before symptoms appear.
The company has been incubating new ideas in its innovation lab.

senses.meaning: Giống (động vật, đặc biệt giống được lai tạo)
examples: The Labrador is one of the most popular dog breeds in the world.
What breed is your horse?
They developed a new breed of cattle resistant to tropical diseases.

senses.meaning: Lai tạo, nhân giống (động vật); gây ra (cảm xúc tiêu cực)
examples: She breeds tropical fish as a hobby.
The farm breeds thoroughbred racehorses for competition.
Poverty and inequality breed resentment and social unrest.

senses.meaning: Nông dân nghèo (bối cảnh lịch sử hoặc đang phát triển)
examples: Peasants in medieval Europe paid taxes and labour to the local lord.
Millions of peasants were forced to leave their land during the famine.
The revolution was led by poor peasants and factory workers.

note: Có thể mang hàm ý miệt thị khi dùng trong ngữ cảnh hiện đại để chỉ người kém giáo dục.

senses.meaning: (Động vật) gặm cỏ, ăn cỏ; chăn thả gia súc
examples: Cattle grazed peacefully in the meadow all afternoon.
Sheep have been grazing on these hills for centuries.
Farmers graze their herds on communal land during summer.

senses.meaning: Xước nhẹ bề mặt; sướt qua
examples: The bullet grazed his arm, leaving only a minor wound.
She grazed her knee badly when she fell off the bicycle.
The car just grazed the bollard as it turned the corner.

note: Hai nghĩa hoàn toàn khác: (1) súc vật gặm cỏ; (2) xước nhẹ bề mặt.

senses.meaning: (Đất) có thể canh tác, thích hợp để trồng trọt
examples: Only 10% of the country's total land is arable.
Arable farming has declined as land is converted to pasture.
They decided to convert the arable land into a nature reserve.

senses.meaning: Canh tác, trồng trọt; nuôi dưỡng (mối quan hệ, kỹ năng, thái độ)
examples: Local farmers cultivate rice in the flooded paddies during monsoon season.
She cultivated a friendship with her neighbour over many years.
He spent years cultivating his knowledge of classical music.

note: Dùng cả nghĩa đen (canh tác đất) lẫn nghĩa bóng (vun đắp mối quan hệ/kỹ năng).

senses.meaning: Gặt, thu hoạch; gặt hái kết quả
examples: Farmers reap the wheat in late summer after months of hard work.
The company is now reaping the benefits of its early investment.
You reap what you sow — choices today shape outcomes tomorrow.

note: 'You reap what you sow' = gieo gì gặt nấy — thành ngữ phổ biến.

senses.meaning: Chín, trở nên chín; làm cho chín (trái cây, phomai, rượu)
examples: Tomatoes ripen best in warm, sunny conditions.
Bananas ripen quickly at room temperature.
The cheese needs to ripen for at least six months to develop its flavour.

note: Dùng cho trái cây, ngũ cốc, phomai, và rượu vang.

senses.meaning: Cằn cỗi, không màu mỡ (đất); vô sinh (người/động vật); thiếu vắng (ý tưởng)
examples: The desert landscape was utterly barren and devoid of life.
After years of drought, the once-fertile fields became barren.
He described the meeting as a barren exchange of empty promises.

note: Đối lập: 'fertile'. Cũng dùng nghĩa bóng: 'a barren period' = thời kỳ không sản xuất được gì.

senses.meaning: Thuộc về/liên quan đến nông nghiệp
examples: Agricultural land makes up 40% of the country's total area.
The agricultural sector employs millions of people in developing countries.
New agricultural techniques have dramatically improved crop yields.

senses.meaning: Phân hữu cơ, mùn compost (từ chất thải hữu cơ)
examples: She added compost to the garden to improve the soil quality.
The kitchen waste was turned into compost over several months.
Compost is a natural, eco-friendly alternative to chemical fertilizers.

senses.meaning: Làm phân compost từ chất thải hữu cơ
examples: Many households now compost their food scraps and garden waste.
He composted the fallen leaves into a rich mulch for the garden.
Composting reduces the amount of organic waste sent to landfill.
